subject: Economics
title: Cost for firms in a boom

stages.name: Cost for firms in a boom
stages.title: Cost for firms in a boom
stages.sub: Why a booming economy that helps firms' sales can also squeeze their margins.

steps.q: The economy is booming and every firm wants more raw materials and machinery at once. What happens to how hard firms compete for these inputs?
steps.right: They compete harder to get hold of them
steps.wrong: They stop needing as many of them
steps.hint: Everyone wants more of the same inputs at the same time.

steps.q: Factories that make raw materials and machinery can only expand production so fast, even when every firm suddenly wants more. What does that mean for how much is actually available this year?
steps.right: It stays limited in the short run
steps.wrong: It expands just as fast as demand rises
steps.hint: Building new factories and training more workers takes time, not just wanting more.

steps.q: With many firms hiring at once but only a limited pool of skilled workers, what do firms have to do to attract staff?
steps.right: Offer higher pay to win workers
steps.wrong: Offer lower pay since workers are keen to join
steps.hint: If lots of firms chase the same small pool of workers, what happens to what employers must offer?
